Main.sentence: The 2005 American League Championship Series ( ALCS ), the second round of the ___E:American League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_League)___ side in ___E:Major League Baseball U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball)___ 's ___E:2005 postseason U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Major_League_Baseball_postseason)___ , which determined the 2005 American League champion, matched the Central Division champion and top-seeded ___E:Chicago White Sox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_White_Sox)___ against the West Division champion and second-seeded ___E:Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Angels_of_Anaheim)___ .
The White Sox, by virtue of having the best record in the AL during the 2005 season, had the home-field advantage.

The White Sox won the series four games to one to become the American League champions, and faced the ___E:Houston Astros U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Astros)___ in the ___E:2005 World Series U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Series)___ , in which the White Sox swept the Astros in four games to win their first World Series championship in ___E:88 years U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1917_World_Series)___ ; as a result of the ___E:2005 All-Star Game U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game)___ played in Detroit, Michigan at ___E:Comerica Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comerica_Park)___ on July 12, the White Sox had home-field advantage in the World Series.

The series was notable both for a controversial call in Game 2 of the series, and the outstanding pitching and durability of Chicago's starting rotation, pitching four consecutive complete games; the .mw-parser-output .frac{white-space:nowrap}.mw-parser-output .frac .num,.mw-parser-output .frac .den{font-size:80%;line-height:0;vertical-align:super}.mw-parser-output .frac .den{vertical-align:sub}.mw-parser-output .sr-only{border:0;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);clip-path:polygon(0px 0px,0px 0px,0px 0px);height:1px;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;padding:0;position:absolute;width:1px} +2⁄3 of an inning ___E:Neal Cotts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neal_Cotts)___ pitched in the first game was the only work the White Sox bullpen saw the entire series.

The White Sox and Angels were victorious in the ___E:AL Division Series U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_American_League_Division_Series)___ (ALDS), with the White Sox defeating the defending World Champion and wild card qualifier ___E:Boston Red Sox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox)___ three games to none, and the Angels defeating the Eastern Division champion ___E:New York Yankees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees)___ three games to two. It was the first ALCS since ___E:2002 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_American_League_Championship_Series)___ not to feature the Red Sox or the Yankees.
Chicago won the series, 4–1.
In the series opener, the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim won 3–2 in their third game in as many nights and as many cities.

The Angels took the lead in the second inning on a ___E:Garret Anderson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garret_Anderson)___ leadoff home run. Next inning, ___E:Steve Finley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Finley)___ and ___E:Adam Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Kennedy)___ hit back-to-back leadoff singles and advanced one base each on ___E:Chone Figgins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chone_Figgins)___ 's sacrifice bunt. ___E:Orlando Cabrera U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Cabrera)___ 's single and ___E:Vladimir Guerrero U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Guerrero)___ 's groundout scored a run each. White Sox starter ___E:José Contreras U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Contreras)___ allowed no more runs, going 8+1⁄3 innings.
In the bottom of the inning, Joe Crede's home run off of Paul Byrd put the Sox on the board.
Next inning, Chicago's Carl Everett singled with one out, moved to second on a groundout, and scored on A. J.

Pierzynski's single to make it a one-run game. However, neither team would score for the rest of the game. It was the first time in six tries that the Angels won a Game 1 under manager Mike Scioscia, despite having won the World Series in 2002. This turned out to be the only game the White Sox would lose in the entire postseason.
Then-Senator and future President of the United States ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ threw out the ceremonial first pitch.

Behind a complete game from ___E:Mark Buehrle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Buehrle)___ and a now infamous strikeout in the bottom of the ninth, the White Sox evened the series at a game apiece.

In the bottom of the first, ___E:Scott Podsednik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Podsednik)___ reached second on an error, moved to third on a sacrifice bunt, and scored on ___E:Jermaine Dye U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jermaine_Dye)___ 's ground out. ___E:Jarrod Washburn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarrod_Washburn)___ and two relievers held the Sox scoreless over the next seven innings while ___E:Robb Quinlan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robb_Quinlan)___ 's fifth inning home run tied the game. It remained tied until the bottom of the ninth.

With two strikes, ___E:A. J. Pierzynski U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._J._Pierzynski)___ swung and missed at a low pitch from Angels pitcher ___E:Kelvim Escobar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvim_Escobar)___ for strike three. ___E:Josh Paul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Paul_(baseball))___ , the Angels catcher, rolled the ball to the mound and left the infield.

Pierzynski realized strike three had been called, so he ran to first base in case the umpire ruled that the catcher had not legally caught the strike-three pitch  (see ___E:Uncaught third strike U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncaught_third_strike)___ rule).

In a controversial call, home-plate umpire ___E:Doug Eddings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doug_Eddings)___ ruled that the ball hit the ground before going into the catcher's glove and signalled strike 3 but did not call him out,  so the pitch was considered uncaught and Pierzynski was safe at first.

A ___E:pinch-runner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinch-runner)___ , ___E:Pablo Ozuna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Ozuna)___ , stole second base. ___E:Third baseman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_baseman)___ ___E:Joe Crede U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Crede)___ delivered a base hit three pitches later, scoring Ozuna for the winning run.

Chicago jumped to a 3−0 lead in the first inning off of ___E:John Lackey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lackey)___ as the series moved west to Anaheim. ___E:Scott Podsednik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Podsednik)___ hit a leadoff single, moved to second on a sacrifice bunt and came home on ___E:Jermaine Dye U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jermaine_Dye)___ 's single before ___E:Paul Konerko U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Konerko)___ 's two-run home run capped the scoring. ___E:Tadahito Iguchi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tadahito_Iguchi)___ singled to lead off the third, moved to second on a walk, and scored on ___E:Carl Everett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Everett)___ 's single.

Two innings later, Iguchi doubled with one out and scored on Konerko's two-out single to put Chicago up 5−0. A two-run home run by ___E:Orlando Cabrera U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Cabrera)___ in the sixth cut the lead to 5−2, but it would not be enough as the White Sox took the series lead, two games to one, with ___E:Jon Garland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Garland)___ pitching a ___E:complete game U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complete_game)___ .
The visitors again jumped to a 3−0 lead in the first.

Angel starter ___E:Ervin Santana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ervin_Santana)___ walked ___E:Scott Podsednik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Podsednik)___ and hit ___E:Tadahito Iguchi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tadahito_Iguchi)___ before ___E:Paul Konerko U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Konerko)___ , after a disputed check swing on a 2–2 pitch, homered for the second straight game. The Angels cut it to 3−1 in the second when ___E:Darin Erstad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darin_Erstad)___ walked with one out, moved to third on ___E:Casey Kotchman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Kotchman)___ 's single and White Sox pitcher ___E:Freddy Garcia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddy_Garc%C3%ADa)___ 's throwing error to first, then scored on ___E:Bengie Molina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengie_Molina)___ 's single.

With men on first and third, ___E:Steve Finley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Finley)___ hit a ground ball to second for an inning-ending double play, but argued that Sox catcher ___E:A. J. Pierzynski U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._J._Pierzynski)___ had interfered with his swing.

Chicago got that run back when ___E:Jermaine Dye U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jermaine_Dye)___ reached on shortstop ___E:Orlando Cabrera U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Cabrera)___ 's throwing error to first, stole second, and scored on ___E:Carl Everett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Everett)___ 's base hit. Pierzynski's home run next inning made it 5−1. In the bottom of the inning, Angel ___E:Garret Anderson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garret_Anderson)___ singled with one out and scored on Kotchman's two-out double, but in the fifth, Podsednik drew a leadoff walk and after ___E:Scot Shields U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scot_Shields)___ relieved Santana, stole second and scored on Everett's single. ___E:Esteban Yan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esteban_Yan)___ walked Everett to lead off the eighth, allowed a subsequent double to ___E:Aaron Rowand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rowand)___ followed by ___E:Joe Crede U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Crede)___ 's two-run single to put the Sox up 8−2. García pitched the White Sox's third straight complete game, helping put them one win from their first ___E:World Series U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Series)___ visit since ___E:1959 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_World_Series)___ .

Still on the road, Chicago struck first in Game 5 when ___E:Aaron Rowand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rowand)___ hit a leadoff ground-rule double in the second off of ___E:Paul Byrd U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Byrd)___ , moved to third on a sacrifice bunt, then scored on ___E:Joe Crede U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Crede)___ 's sacrifice fly. But the Angels tied it in the third when ___E:Juan Rivera U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Rivera_(baseball))___ hit a leadoff double, moved to third on pitcher ___E:Jose Contreras U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Contreras)___ 's pickoff attempt error, and scored on ___E:Adam Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Kennedy)___ 's single.

In the top of the fifth, ___E:Juan Uribe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Uribe)___ doubled and scored on ___E:Jermaine Dye U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jermaine_Dye)___ 's single, but in the bottom of the inning, Kennedy hit a leadoff single and scored on ___E:Chone Figgins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chone_Figgins)___ 's double.

Figgins scored on a ___E:Garret Anderson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garret_Anderson)___ sacrifice fly to put the Angels up 3−2. Crede's leadoff home run in the seventh off of ___E:Kelvim Escobar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvim_Escobar)___ tied the game. Next inning, Escobar walked Rowand with two outs and an error moved him to second. ___E:Francisco Rodriguez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Rodr%C3%ADguez_(Venezuelan_pitcher))___ relieved Escobar and Crede greeted him with an RBI single to put the White Sox up 4−3. Chicago captured its first American League pennant since ___E:1959 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_World_Series)___ .

This marked the first time in ___E:77 years U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1928_World_Series)___ that a team threw four straight complete-game victories in the playoffs, becoming the first time it was done by four different pitchers since the ___E:Chicago Cubs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1907_Chicago_Cubs_season)___ did it in the ___E:1907 World Series U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1907_World_Series)___ .

Konerko was named the ALCS MVP. He finished the series ___E:batting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batting_average_(baseball))___ .286, with two ___E:home runs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_run)___ and seven ___E:RBIs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run_batted_in)___ .

His two home runs came in the first innings of Games 3 and 4; he became only the third player in Major League history to hit homers in the first inning of consecutive playoff games, the other two having been ___E:Dan Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Ford)___ during the ___E:1979 ALCS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_American_League_Championship_Series)___ and ___E:Carlos Beltrán U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Beltr%C3%A1n)___ during the ___E:2004 NLCS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_National_League_Championship_Series)___ .

___E:Doug Eddings' U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doug_Eddings)___ controversial call in Game 2, when he ruled that a strikeout to ___E:A. J. Pierzynski U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._J._Pierzynski)___ by ___E:Kelvim Escobar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvim_Escobar)___ had not been legally caught (an ___E:uncaught third strike U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncaught_third_strike)___ ) by catcher ___E:Josh Paul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Paul_(baseball))___ but made no audible call that the ball hit the ground, proved to be the most pivotal point in the series.

At the team's ten-year anniversary in 2015, White Sox chairman ___E:Jerry Reinsdorf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Reinsdorf)___ acknowledged that losing home-field advantage and going down 0-2 in a best-of-seven series would have been too difficult of a hole to climb out of. Catcher A. J.

Pierzynski, who was at the center of the call, said the year before when he was in ___E:San Francisco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_San_Francisco_Giants_season)___ , he was on the other end of that same type of play. Both ___E:Paul Konerko U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Konerko)___ and general manager ___E:Kenny Williams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Williams_(baseball))___ believed that Eddings likely got the call wrong.

According to umpire supervisor ___E:Rich Rieker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_Rieker)___ , the replays showed "there was definitely a change in direction there" indicating the ball touched the ground and felt, at best, the replay was inconclusive.

Pierzynski was booed every time he played in Anaheim until his retirement for his role in the controversy.

Major League Baseball did not adopt ___E:review via instant replay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instant_replay_in_Major_League_Baseball)___ on calls such as this until the ___E:2014 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Major_League_Baseball_season)___ season.

As of 2024, the White Sox in the 2005 ALCS are the only team to throw four complete games in a playoff series since the beginning of league championship series play in 1969. Prior to that, several teams had done so when the World Series was the only round of the MLB postseason.
As of the 2024 season, this is the last White Sox' AL Championship Series appearance.
